projection.title: Fourier pairing for a finite measure and Schwartz data
projection.statement: Assume Countable Choice. Let $\mu$ be a finite complex Borel measure on $\mathbb R^n$ and let $F,G\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^n)$. (i) $\int_{\mathbb R^n}(G\mu)^\vee(x)\overline{F(x)}\,dx=\int_{\mathbb R^n}G(\omega)\overline{\widehat F(\omega)}\,d\mu(\omega)$, where $(G\mu)^\vee(x)=\int e^{2\pi ix\cdot\omega}G(\omega)\,d\mu(\omega)$. (ii) Writing $\check\mu(x):=\widehat\mu(-x)=\int e^{2\pi ix\cdot\omega}\,d\mu(\omega)$, one has $(\widehat F\,\mu)^\vee=F*\check\mu$ as everywhere-defined bounded continuous functions. (iii) $|\check\mu(x)|\le|\mu|(\mathbb R^n)$ for every $x$, and $\check\mu$ is uniformly continuous.

references.title: Mark Williams, Notes on harmonic analysis, §11.1–11.4, printed pp. 71–77
Thomas H. Wolff, Lectures in Harmonic Analysis (editor-hosted notes, March 2002), §6–§7, printed pp. 33–49

projection.strategy: Fubini on the product $\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^n$ against the finite measure $\mu$, the unit modulus of the exponential, and Schwartz inversion for (ii); the uniform-continuity clause is the finite-measure transform theorem applied to the reflection of $\mu$.

projection.title: TT-star reduces extension to convolution with the surface-measure transform
projection.statement: Assume Countable Choice. Let $\mu$ be a finite complex Borel measure on $\mathbb R^n$, let $E_\mu g=(g\mu)^\vee$ for $g\in L^1(\mu)\cap L^2(\mu)$, and let $E_\mu^*F$ be the restriction of $\widehat F$ to $\operatorname{supp}\mu$ for $F\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^n)$. Then $E_\mu E_\mu^*F=F*\check\mu$ for every $F\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^n)$, and for every $1\le p\le\infty$, $\|\widehat F\|_{L^2(\mu)}^2=\langle(\widehat F\mu)^\vee,F\rangle=\langle F*\check\mu,F\rangle\le\|F\|_{L^p}\|F*\check\mu\|_{L^{p'}}$. In particular, for a compact hypersurface $S$ with surface measure $\sigma$, a bound on $\|F*\check\sigma\|_{L^{p'}}$ bounds $\|\widehat F\|_{L^2(\sigma)}$.

references.title: Thomas H. Wolff, Lectures in Harmonic Analysis (editor-hosted notes, March 2002), §6–§7, printed pp. 33–49
Mark Williams, Notes on harmonic analysis, §11.1–11.4, printed pp. 71–77

projection.strategy: Apply the pairing identity with $G=\widehat F$ to identify the squared $L^2(\mu)$ norm with $\langle(\widehat F\mu)^\vee,F\rangle$, then the convolution identity to replace $(\widehat F\mu)^\vee$ by $F*\check\mu$, and Holder to bound the pairing.

projection.title: Knapp rules out extension below the Tomas exponent
projection.statement: Let $n\ge2$ and let $q<2(n+1)/(n-1)$. For every $C>0$ there is $\delta\in(0,1]$ such that the spherical cap data $g=\mathbf 1_{C_\delta}\in L^2(\sigma)$ satisfy $\|Eg\|_{L^q(\mathbb R^n)}>C\|g\|_{L^2(\sigma)}$. Hence no extension estimate $E:L^2(S^{n-1})\to L^q(\mathbb R^n)$ holds below the Stein-Tomas exponent, and consequently no restriction estimate $R:L^p(\mathbb R^n)\to L^2(S^{n-1})$ holds for $p>2(n+1)/(n+3)$.

references.title: Thomas H. Wolff, Lectures in Harmonic Analysis (editor-hosted notes, March 2002), §6–§7, printed pp. 33–49
Terence Tao, Math 247B Lecture Notes 8: Oscillatory integrals, §§1–4, pp. 1–13

projection.strategy: Combine the cap concentration with the slab volume, compute $\|Eg\|_q\gtrsim\delta^{n-1-(n+1)/q}$ and $\|g\|_2\asymp\delta^{(n-1)/2}$, and let $\delta\downarrow0$ for $q$ below the Tomas exponent.

projection.title: The one-dimensional endpoint estimate on a bounded interval
projection.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice through the ACL interface of [[thm-acl-characterisation-of-w-one-p]]. Let $I=(a,b)$ be a bounded open interval, $1\le p<\infty$, $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, and let $u\in W^{1,p}(I;\mathbb K)$ with weak derivative $u'$ and unique absolutely continuous representative $u^*$ ([[cor-one-dimensional-w-one-p-functions-have-absolutely-continuous-representatives]]). Then for every $0<\varepsilon<b-a$: (i) if $1<p<\infty$, $|u^*(a)|^p\le 2^{p-1}\bigl(\varepsilon^{-1}\int_a^{a+\varepsilon}|u^*|^p+\varepsilon^{p-1}\int_a^{a+\varepsilon}|u'|^p\bigr)$, and the same inequality holds at $b$ with $(b-\varepsilon,b)$; (ii) if $p=1$, $|u^*(a)|\le\varepsilon^{-1}\int_a^{a+\varepsilon}|u^*|+\int_a^{a+\varepsilon}|u'|$, and likewise at $b$. The endpoint values are those of the absolutely continuous representative and do not depend on the chosen representative of the class.
projection.strategy: For a.e. $t\in(a,a+\varepsilon)$ the absolutely continuous representative satisfies $u^*(a)-u^*(t)=-\int_a^t u'$, hence $|u^*(a)|\le|u^*(t)|+\int_a^{a+\varepsilon}|u'|$. For $p>1$ raise this to the $p$-th power with $|x+y|^p\le 2^{p-1}(|x|^p+|y|^p)$, integrate in $t$ over $(a,a+\varepsilon)$, divide by $\varepsilon$, and bound $\int_a^{a+\varepsilon}\bigl(\int_a^{a+\varepsilon}|u'|\bigr)^p=\varepsilon\bigl(\int_a^{a+\varepsilon}|u'|\bigr)^p\le\varepsilon^p\int_a^{a+\varepsilon}|u'|^p$ by Holder. For $p=1$ integrate the unsquared inequality. The capital-$C$ form used later is $\varepsilon|u^*(a)|^p\le C_p\bigl(\int_a^{a+\varepsilon}|u^*|^p+\varepsilon^p\int_a^{a+\varepsilon}|u'|^p\bigr)$. The ACL and FTC interfaces carry the Axiom of Choice; no further choice is used.

projection.title: The half-space trace estimate and the half-space trace operator
projection.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $n\ge2$, $d=n-1$, $1\le p<\infty$, $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, and let $H=\{x=(x',x_n)\in\mathbb R^n:x_n>0\}$ with $\partial H=\mathbb R^d\times\{0\}$. (i) For every $u\in C(\overline H)\cap W^{1,p}(H;\mathbb K)$ with compact support, the classical boundary function $g=u(\cdot,0)$ satisfies $|g(x')|^p\le p\int_0^\infty|u(x',t)|^{p-1}\,|\partial_nu(x',t)|\,dt$ for a.e. $x'\in\mathbb R^d$, hence $\|g\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^d)}^p\le p\,\|u\|_{L^p(H)}^{p-1}\|\partial_nu\|_{L^p(H)}\le p\,\|u\|_{W^{1,p}(H)}^p$. For every $h>0$ the strip form $h\,|g(x')|^p\le C_p\bigl(\int_0^h|u(x',t)|^pdt+h^p\int_0^h|\partial_nu(x',t)|^pdt\bigr)$ holds for a.e. $x'$. (ii) There is a unique bounded linear operator $T_+:W^{1,p}(H;\mathbb K)\to L^p(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb K)$ with $T_+u=u(\cdot,0)$ for every compactly supported $u\in C(\overline H)\cap W^{1,p}(H)$, and $\|T_+u\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^d)}\le C(n,p)\|u\|_{W^{1,p}(H)}$; it is the unique bounded extension of classical restriction, and $T_+u$ depends only on the a.e. class of $u$.
projection.strategy: For (i), fix a representative continuous on $\overline H$; for a.e. $x'$ the section $t\mapsto u(x',t)$ is absolutely continuous on $(0,\infty)$ by the ACL theorem, and since $u$ has compact support, $|g(x')|^p=-\int_0^\infty\partial_t(|u(x',t)|^p)\,dt=-p\int_0^\infty|u|^{p-2}\operatorname{Re}(\overline u\,\partial_nu)dt\le p\int_0^\infty|u|^{p-1}|\partial_nu|\,dt$. Integrate in $x'$, apply Holder with exponents $p/(p-1)$ and $p$, and use $\|\partial_nu\|_p\le\|u\|_{W^{1,p}(H)}$. The strip form integrates the one-dimensional endpoint estimate [[lem-one-dimensional-sobolev-endpoint-estimate]] along the normal section. For (ii), classical restriction is defined on compactly supported smooth functions and is uniformly bounded by (i); that subspace is dense in $W^{1,p}(H)$ because a cutoff in $|x|$ reduces to the bounded domains $H\cap B_R$, where [[thm-smooth-up-to-the-boundary-density-on-smooth-domains]] applies. Apply the bounded-extension property of a dense subspace ([[thm-completion-universal-property-for-bounded-linear-maps]]); uniqueness is immediate. The Axiom of Choice is carried through the density interface used to reach all classes.

projection.title: The trace commutes with smooth cutoffs and is chart local
projection.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a bounded $C^1$ domain, $1\le p<\infty$, and let $T$ be the trace operator of [[thm-lp-trace-operator-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]]. (i) If $\eta\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb K)$, then $T(\eta u)=(\eta|_{\partial\Omega})\,Tu$ in $L^p(\partial\Omega)$ for every $u\in W^{1,p}(\Omega)$, and $\|T(\eta u)\|_{L^p(\partial\Omega)}\le C_\eta\|u\|_{W^{1,p}(\Omega)}$. (ii) If $\Omega'\subseteq\Omega$ is open and $\partial\Omega\cap\partial\Omega'$ is relatively open in $\partial\Omega$, then $(Tu)|_{\partial\Omega\cap\partial\Omega'}=T_{\Omega'}(u|_{\Omega'})$ a.e. for every $u\in W^{1,p}(\Omega)$, where $T_{\Omega'}$ is the trace operator relative to $\Omega'$; in particular the trace is local and compatible with restrictions to subdomains. (iii) If a boundary chart $\Phi$ flattens a neighbourhood of a boundary point, then for $u$ supported in the interior of that chart the transported trace equals $T_+(u\circ\Phi^{-1})$ and the corresponding boundary $L^p$ norms agree up to the chart Jacobian.
projection.strategy: Both identities are classical for smooth functions. Approximate a general $u$ by restrictions of $C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^n)$ functions in the $W^{1,p}$ norm ([[thm-smooth-up-to-the-boundary-density-on-smooth-domains]]), use the product rule [[lem-weak-leibniz-rule-with-a-smooth-factor]] and the continuity of $T$ to pass to the limit in (i); the multiplier $\eta|_{\partial\Omega}$ is continuous on the compact boundary, and Holder gives the stated bound, using [[lem-bounded-restriction-and-cutoff-localisation-in-sobolev-spaces]] for the localisation. Part (ii) follows by testing with cutoffs supported in the common boundary neighbourhood and applying the chartwise definition in part (iii); the transported boundary measure is the chart surface measure, which is chart independent by the page's surface-measure convention. The Axiom of Choice is carried by the density interface.

projection.title: The Gauss-Green integration-by-parts formula with Sobolev traces
projection.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge2$, be a bounded $C^1$ domain, $1<p<\infty$, $p'=p/(p-1)$, $u\in W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$, $v\in W^{1,p'}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$, and let $T$ be the trace of [[thm-lp-trace-operator-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]] with $
u$ the outward normal of [[def-bounded-c-one-domain-boundary-charts-and-outward-normal]]. Then for every $i=1,\dots,n$, $\int_\Omega u\,\partial_iv\,dx=-\int_\Omega(\partial_iu)v\,dx+\int_{\partial\Omega}(Tu)(Tv)\,
u_i\,dS$, and all three integrals are finite. If $u,v\in C^1(\overline\Omega)$, the boundary term is the classical $\int_{\partial\Omega}uv\,
u_i\,dS$ of the divergence theorem [[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-c-one-euclidean-domains]] applied to the field $uv\,e_i$; when $u=\partial_
u w$ this is the classical normal-derivative boundary term of [[def-classical-normal-derivative]].
projection.strategy: For $u,v\in C^1(\overline\Omega)$ the identity is the divergence theorem applied to the field $uv\,e_i$ on the bounded $C^1$ domain. For general $u,v$ choose $u_k\to u$ in $W^{1,p}(\Omega)$ and $v_k\to v$ in $W^{1,p'}(\Omega)$ with $u_k,v_k$ restrictions of $C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^n)$ functions ([[thm-smooth-up-to-the-boundary-density-on-smooth-domains]]), so that $Tu_k\to Tu$ and $Tv_k\to Tv$ in the respective boundary $L^p$ spaces. The volume pairings converge by Holder, $\int_\Omega|u_k\partial_iv_k-u\partial_iv|\le\|u_k-u\|_p\|\partial_iv_k\|_{p'}+\|u\|_p\|\partial_iv_k-\partial_iv\|_{p'}\to0$, and the boundary pairings converge by Holder on $\partial\Omega$ with exponents $p,p'$ ([[thm-holder-inequality-for-integrals]]), the boundary measure being finite. All boundary terms are in $L^1(\partial\Omega)$ since $Tu\in L^p$ and $Tv\in L^{p'}$. The Axiom of Choice is carried by the density and trace interfaces.

projection.title: The kernel of the trace is the closure of the test functions
projection.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge2$, be a bounded $C^1$ domain and $1\le p<\infty$. Then the kernel of the trace operator of [[thm-lp-trace-operator-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]] equals the zero-boundary Sobolev space: $\{u\in W^{1,p}(\Omega):Tu=0\}=W_0^{1,p}(\Omega)$, the $W^{1,p}$-closure of $C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ ([[def-wkp-zero-as-a-sobolev-closure]]).
projection.strategy: Forward: for $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ the classical restriction to $\partial\Omega$ vanishes, so $T\varphi=0$ by [[lem-sobolev-trace-agrees-with-continuous-boundary-values]], and $T$ is continuous, so the identity passes to the $W^{1,p}$-closure. Conversely let $Tu=0$. Localise with the finite ambient partition of [[lem-finite-ambient-partitions-for-euclidean-boundary-integration]] and an interior cutoff, and for each boundary piece $w=\chi_ju$ flatten to a compactly supported $W^{1,p}(H)$ function with zero flat trace ([[lem-c-k-boundary-flattening-preserves-wkp-locally]], [[lem-trace-commutes-with-smooth-boundary-cutoffs-and-charts]]). Define $\bar w$ on $\mathbb R^n$ to be $w$ on $H$ and $0$ below the boundary. The half-space case of [[thm-sobolev-gauss-green-formula-on-c-one-domains]] (applied on a large half-ball containing the support) shows, for every test function $\varphi$, $\int_{\mathbb R^n}\bar w\,\partial_i\varphi=-\int_{\mathbb R^n}\bar v_i\,\varphi$ where $\bar v_i$ is the zero extension of $\partial_iw$: the boundary term at $x_n=0$ contains the flat trace $T_+w=0$ and the spherical part is outside the support. Hence $\bar w\in W^{1,p}(\mathbb R^n)$ with the zero-extended weak derivatives. Translate, $w_\varepsilon(x):=\bar w(x-\varepsilon e_n)$, so that $w_\varepsilon\to w$ in $W^{1,p}(H)$ by translation continuity, and mollify at scale $\delta<\varepsilon/2$: $\rho_\delta*w_\varepsilon\in C_c^\infty(H)$ with $\rho_\delta*w_\varepsilon\to w$ in $W^{1,p}(H)$ ([[cor-compactly-supported-smooth-functions-are-dense-in-wkp-of-rn]]). Pulling these approximations back through the chart gives $C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ functions converging to $\chi_ju$, and the interior piece is mollified directly; a finite sum of $C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ approximations converges to $u$, so $u\in W_0^{1,p}(\Omega)$. The Axiom of Choice is carried by the density, flattening and partition interfaces; the extension-by-zero step is otherwise explicit.

projection.title: The Gagliardo-Slobodeckij space on Euclidean space
projection.statement: Assume Countable Choice for the measure interfaces. Let $d\ge1$, $0<s<1$, $1\le p<\infty$ and $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. For a measurable $g:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb K$ put $[g]_{s,p}:=\bigl(\int_{\mathbb R^d}\int_{\mathbb R^d}|g(x)-g(y)|^p|x-y|^{-d-sp}\,dx\,dy\bigr)^{1/p}\in[0,\infty]$, with the integrand understood as $0$ on the diagonal $x=y$. The Gagliardo-Slobodeckij space is $W^{s,p}(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb K):=\{g\in L^p(\mathbb R^d):[g]_{s,p}<\infty\}$, normed by $\|g\|_{W^{s,p}}:=\|g\|_{L^p}+[g]_{s,p}$. The seminorm and the space are meant to depend only on the almost-everywhere class; representative independence is recorded as the first clause of the well-definedness lemma on this page. On this page the exponent used is $s=\theta:=1-1/p\in(0,1)$, which is the trace exponent for $1<p<\infty$.
projection.strategy: Unpack the double integral as an integral over the completed product measure on $\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R^d$ ([[thm-tonelli-and-fubini-for-completed-product-measures]]); the diagonal is a null set, so the convention is harmless, and the integral is a nonnegative extended integral of a measurable function ([[def-nonnegative-lebesgue-integral]]). Membership and norm are stated on classes ([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]); representative independence is not assumed here but proved as the first clause of [[lem-slobodeckij-seminorm-is-well-defined]]. Only the countable-choice measure interfaces are used; the definition itself is choice free.

projection.title: The coordinate-direction form of the Slobodeckij seminorm
projection.statement: Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\ge1$, $0<s<1$, $1\le p<\infty$, and let $g$ be measurable. Then, with $e_1,\dots,e_d$ the canonical basis, $[g]_{s,p}^p\asymp_{d,p,s}\sum_{i=1}^d\int_0^\infty h^{-1-sp}\int_{\mathbb R^d}|g(x+he_i)-g(x)|^p\,dx\,dh$, in the sense that both sides are finite simultaneously and the two quantities are comparable by constants depending only on $d,p,s$. For the trace exponent $s=\theta=1-1/p$ the weight is $h^{-p}$, because $1+p\theta=p$.
projection.strategy: By translation invariance of Lebesgue measure ([[thm-integrals-are-invariant-under-measure-preserving-maps]]) substitute $y=x+h$ in the inner integral, so $[g]_{s,p}^p=\int_{\mathbb R^d}\|\tau_hg-g\|_{L^p}^p|h|^{-d-sp}dh$. Polar coordinates ([[thm-polar-coordinates-formula-for-lebesgue-measure]]) turn this into the integral over radii of the spherical mean of $\|\tau_{r\omega}g-g\|_p^p$ against $r^{-1-sp}dr$. Cover the unit sphere by the finitely many coordinate caps $\{|\omega_i|\ge c_d\}$; on a cap with $\omega_i\ge c_d$ the increment $h=r\omega$ satisfies $r\le c_d^{-1}h_i$ with $h_i=r\omega_i$, so the full increment is controlled by the coordinate increment $h_ie_i$ plus the tangential remainder of size $O(r)$, and iterating over the $d$ caps gives the upper comparison; the lower comparison is immediate because the coordinate directions form a subset of all directions. The identity $1+p\theta=p$ at $\theta=1-1/p$ converts the weight. Only countable-choice measure interfaces are used.

projection.title: The Hardy inequality for the averaging operator on the half-line
projection.statement: Let $1<p<\infty$ and let $f:(0,\infty)\to[0,\infty]$ be measurable. Then $\bigl(\int_0^\infty\bigl(t^{-1}\int_0^tf(s)\,ds\bigr)^pdt\bigr)^{1/p}\le\frac{p}{p-1}\bigl(\int_0^\infty f^p\bigr)^{1/p}$; equivalently $\int_0^\infty t^{-p}\bigl(\int_0^tf\bigr)^pdt\le\bigl(\frac{p}{p-1}\bigr)^p\int_0^\infty f^p$, with $+\infty$ on either side allowed, and the constant $p/(p-1)$ is sharp. The same inequality holds on $(0,T)$ for every $0<T<\infty$ when $f$ is supported in $(0,T)$, with the same constant.
projection.strategy: Assume first that $f$ is continuous with compact support and put $F(t)=\int_0^tf$. Integrate by parts on $(\delta,T)$ against the primitive of $t^{-p}$, namely $-t^{1-p}/(p-1)$: $\int_\delta^TF^pt^{-p}dt=\bigl[-F^pt^{1-p}/(p-1)\bigr]_\delta^T+\frac{p}{p-1}\int_\delta^TF^{p-1}ft^{1-p}dt$. The boundary term at $\delta\downarrow0$ vanishes because $F(t)\le t^{1-1/p}\|f\|_p$ on $(0,t)$, and the term at $T\uparrow\infty$ vanishes because $F$ is eventually constant while $t^{1-p}\to0$. Holders inequality with exponents $p/(p-1)$ and $p$ applied to the product $(F/t)^{p-1}\cdot f$ gives $\int F^{p-1}ft^{1-p}\le\bigl(\int(F/t)^p\bigr)^{(p-1)/p}\|f\|_p$; writing $I=\int_0^\infty(F/t)^pdt$ yields $I\le\frac{p}{p-1}I^{(p-1)/p}\|f\|_p$, hence $I^{1/p}\le\frac{p}{p-1}\|f\|_p$. The general measurable case follows by monotone approximation; the $(0,T)$ case by extending $f$ by zero. The constant is sharp on powers $f(t)=t^{\alpha}$ near the endpoint. No choice beyond Countable Choice for the integral interfaces is used.

projection.title: Compactly supported smooth functions are dense in Slobodeckij spaces
projection.statement: Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\ge1$, $0<s<1$ and $1\le p<\infty$. Then $C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^d)$ is dense in $W^{s,p}(\mathbb R^d)$: for every $g\in W^{s,p}(\mathbb R^d)$ and every $\varepsilon>0$ there is $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^d)$ with $\|g-\varphi\|_{W^{s,p}}<\varepsilon$.
projection.strategy: First truncate: choose $\eta\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^d)$ equal to $1$ near the origin and put $\eta_R(x)=\eta(x/R)$. The functions $\eta_Rg$ converge to $g$ in $L^p$ and in the seminorm: on the region $\{|x|\le R\}$ the functions agree, and the remaining double integral over the escaping region is dominated by $2^{p-1}(|g(x)|^p+|g(y)|^p)$-type integrands whose contribution tends to $0$ by dominated convergence in the double integral. Then mollify: for $\varphi\in W^{s,p}(\mathbb R^d)$ of compact support and the standard mollifier $\rho_\varepsilon$, the difference $|(\rho_\varepsilon*\varphi)(x)-(\rho_\varepsilon*\varphi)(y)|$ is at most $\int\rho_\varepsilon(z)|\varphi(x-z)-\varphi(y-z)|dz$, whence $[\rho_\varepsilon*\varphi]_{s,p}\le[\varphi]_{s,p}$ and $[\rho_\varepsilon*\varphi-\varphi]_{s,p}^p\le\int\rho_\varepsilon(z)\int\int|\varphi(x-z)-\varphi(x)-\varphi(y-z)+\varphi(y)|^p|x-y|^{-d-sp}dxdydz$, which tends to $0$ by translation continuity in $L^p$ ([[thm-translation-is-continuous-in-l-p-for-one-le-p-less-infinity]]) and dominated convergence. Together with [[thm-l-one-approximate-identities-converge-in-l-p]] this gives $\rho_\varepsilon*\varphi\to\varphi$ in $W^{s,p}$. Only countable-choice interfaces are used.

projection.title: The fractional Sobolev space on a compact C^1 boundary
projection.statement: Assume Countable Choice and the boundary conventions of [[def-bounded-c-one-domain-boundary-charts-and-outward-normal]]. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge2$, be a bounded $C^1$ domain, $0<s<1$ and $1\le p<\infty$. Fix a finite family of boundary charts $\Phi_j:U_j\to V_j$, whose restrictions parametrise $\partial\Omega\cap U_j$ over open sets of $\mathbb R^{n-1}$, and a subordinate finite ambient partition $\chi_j$ ([[lem-finite-ambient-partitions-for-euclidean-boundary-integration]]). For a Borel function $g:\partial\Omega\to\mathbb K$ set $\|g\|_{W^{s,p}(\partial\Omega)}:=\sum_j\|(\chi_jg)\circ\Phi_j^{-1}\|_{W^{s,p}(\mathbb R^{n-1})}$, where the chart representation is taken in graph coordinates. Then $W^{s,p}(\partial\Omega;\mathbb K)$ is the set of $L^p(\partial\Omega)$ classes with finite norm. The definition is independent of the atlas and partition up to equivalent norms; the atlas-independence lemma on this page proves the invariance.
projection.strategy: Each chart contributes the Euclidean Slobodeckij norm of [[def-fractional-slobodeckij-space-on-euclidean-space]] applied to the local graph representation; the finite sum over the partition covers the compact boundary, and the surface-measure description of [[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]] fixes which functions are a.e. equal on the boundary. Well-definedness on classes follows from the Euclidean representative independence, and atlas independence is proved separately in [[lem-fractional-boundary-norm-is-independent-of-atlas]]. Countable Choice is carried through the measure interfaces; the finitely many charts and the partition use no further choice.

projection.title: Chart independence of the fractional boundary norm
projection.statement: Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega$ be a bounded $C^1$ domain, $0<s<1$ and $1\le p<\infty$. (i) If $\Psi:V\to V'$ is a $C^1$ diffeomorphism between open subsets of $\mathbb R^{n-1}$ whose derivatives in both directions are bounded, then $\|u\circ\Psi\|_{W^{s,p}(V)}\le C(\Psi,s,p)\|u\|_{W^{s,p}(V')}$ and symmetrically; in particular the Slobodeckij norm is preserved up to equivalence by bi-Lipschitz $C^1$ coordinate changes. (ii) Consequently two finite chart families with subordinate partitions, as in [[def-fractional-sobolev-space-on-a-compact-c-one-boundary]], define equivalent norms on $\partial\Omega$, so $W^{s,p}(\partial\Omega)$ is well defined.
projection.strategy: For (i) split the double integral for $u\circ\Psi$ into pairs with $|x-y|\le r$ and $|x-y|>r$ for a fixed $r>0$. On the near-diagonal part change variables with [[thm-c-one-change-of-variables-for-nonnegative-lebesgue-measurable-functions]] and use the bi-Lipschitz bounds $c_1|x-y|\le|\Psi(x)-\Psi(y)|\le c_2|x-y|$ together with the mean-value bound $|u(\Psi(x))-u(\Psi(y))|^p/|\Psi(x)-\Psi(y)|^{d+sp}\le C|x-y|^{-d-sp}|u|^{\text{difference}}$-type control; on the far part use $|u(\Psi(x))-u(\Psi(y))|^p\le2^{p-1}(|u(\Psi(x))|^p+|u(\Psi(y))|^p)$ and the finiteness of $\int_{|h|>r}|h|^{-d-sp}dh$ together with the change-of-variables formula, giving the $L^p$ term. This is the standard 'split at the length scale' argument; all constants depend on the chart data, $s$, $p$ and the dimension. Part (ii) follows by composing the finitely many chart transitions, each of which is such a diffeomorphism on the overlaps. Only countable-choice measure interfaces are used; the finitely many charts and overlaps are handled without further choice.

projection.title: A bounded right inverse of the half-space trace by normal mollification
projection.statement: Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\ge1$, $1<p<\infty$, $\theta=1-1/p$. Fix $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^d)$ with $\int\varphi=1$, put $\varphi_t(y)=t^{-d}\varphi(y/t)$ and $\psi:=-\sum_i\partial_i(y_i\varphi)$, so that $\int\psi=0$ and $\partial_t(g*\varphi_t)=t^{-1}(g*\psi_t)$; fix $\eta\in C_c^\infty([0,\infty))$ with $\eta\equiv1$ on $[0,1]$ and $\eta\equiv0$ on $[2,\infty)$. For $g\in W^{\theta,p}(\mathbb R^d)$ define $R_+g(x,t):=\eta(t)(g*\varphi_t)(x)$ for $x\in\mathbb R^d$, $t>0$. Then $R_+g\in W^{1,p}(\mathbb R^d\times(0,\infty))$ with $\partial_t(R_+g)=\eta'(t)(g*\varphi_t)+\eta(t)t^{-1}(g*\psi_t)$ and $\partial_{x_i}(R_+g)=\eta(t)(g*\partial_i\varphi_t)$, and $\|R_+g\|_{W^{1,p}}\le C(d,p,\varphi,\eta)\|g\|_{W^{\theta,p}(\mathbb R^d)}$. Moreover $T_+(R_+g)=g$, so $R_+$ is a bounded linear right inverse of the half-space trace $T_+$.
projection.strategy: Define $R_+$ first on the dense subspace $C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^d)$ ([[lem-smooth-compactly-supported-functions-are-dense-in-slobodeckij-spaces]]), where the construction is the source's: with the standard mollifier $\rho$ and $\varphi_t=\rho_t$, put $v(x,t)=g*\rho_{|t|}(x)$ and $R_+g(x,t)=v(x,t)\eta(t)$. This is linear, smooth off $t=0$, continuous up to $t=0$ with $R_+g(\cdot,0)=g$, and Young's inequality gives $\|R_+g\|_p\le C\|g\|_p$; the displayed derivatives are classical. The tangential derivatives are convolutions with the mean-zero kernels $\partial_i\rho_t$, and the normal derivative is a convolution with $\partial_t\rho_t$ plus the term $\eta'(t)(g*\rho_t)$; compact support, boundedness by $Ct^{-d}$ on $B(0,t)$ and the mean-zero property make each of them fall under [[lem-mean-zero-kernel-scale-estimate]], so $\int_0^\infty\|DR_+g(\cdot,t)\|_p^pdt\le C([g]_{\theta,p}^p+\|g\|_p^p)$ and $\|R_+g\|_{W^{1,p}}\le C\|g\|_{W^{\theta,p}}$. The trace identity $T_+(R_+g)=g$ holds by [[lem-sobolev-trace-agrees-with-continuous-boundary-values]]. Finally extend $R_+$ to all of $W^{\theta,p}$ by the bounded-extension property of the dense subspace ([[thm-completion-universal-property-for-bounded-linear-maps]], target $W^{1,p}(H)$ a Banach space); the trace identity extends by continuity. Only countable-choice measure, convolution and completion interfaces are used.

projection.title: The sharp trace theorem: boundedness and range in the fractional space
projection.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge2$, be a bounded $C^1$ domain, $1<p<\infty$ and $\theta=1-1/p$, with $W^{\theta,p}(\partial\Omega)$ as in [[def-fractional-sobolev-space-on-a-compact-c-one-boundary]]. Then the trace operator $T$ of [[thm-lp-trace-operator-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]] satisfies $\|Tu\|_{W^{\theta,p}(\partial\Omega)}\le C(\Omega,p)\|u\|_{W^{1,p}(\Omega)}$ for all $u\in W^{1,p}(\Omega)$, and it is onto: $T(W^{1,p}(\Omega))=W^{\theta,p}(\partial\Omega)$. For $p>1$ the range is a strict subset of $L^p(\partial\Omega)$, and the trace is not a compact operator into $W^{\theta,p}(\partial\Omega)$.
projection.strategy: Boundedness: localise with the finite boundary atlas and partition, flatten each piece to the half-space, and apply the half-space bound [[lem-half-space-trace-has-the-fractional-slobodeckij-bound]]; chart transitions preserve the fractional norm up to equivalence by [[lem-fractional-boundary-norm-is-independent-of-atlas]] and the boundary measure is chart independent, so the chartwise bounds sum to the global one. Surjectivity: for $g\in W^{\theta,p}(\partial\Omega)$ use the local half-space lifts of [[thm-half-space-lift-by-normal-mollification]] on the boundary charts, multiply by a subordinate partition of unity on $\partial\Omega$ and transport with the charts to obtain $u\in W^{1,p}(\Omega)$; the pullbacks of the flat lifts have controlled $W^{1,p}$ norms by the chart-flattening estimate [[lem-c-k-boundary-flattening-preserves-wkp-locally]], the pieces paste by [[lem-trace-commutes-with-smooth-boundary-cutoffs-and-charts]], and $Tu=g$ since each local lift reproduces its cutoff multiple of $g$. Strictness and non-compactness: the trace is onto an infinite-dimensional Banach space, so it cannot be compact; and the range is strictly smaller than $L^p(\partial\Omega)$ because the boundary Slobodeckij seminorm is not controlled by the $L^p$ norm (a jump datum gives a divergent seminorm; the companion page records this). The Axiom of Choice is carried through the density, trace and partition interfaces.

projection.title: A bounded right inverse of the trace, supported in a prescribed collar
projection.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge2$, be a bounded $C^1$ domain, $1<p<\infty$, $\theta=1-1/p$, and let $T$ be the trace. Then there is a bounded linear operator $R:W^{\theta,p}(\partial\Omega)\to W^{1,p}(\Omega)$ with $T\circ R=\mathrm{id}_{W^{\theta,p}(\partial\Omega)}$ and $\|Rg\|_{W^{1,p}(\Omega)}\le C(\Omega,p)\|g\|_{W^{\theta,p}(\partial\Omega)}$. Moreover, for every open neighbourhood $U$ of $\partial\Omega$ in $\mathbb R^n$ there is such an operator $R_U$ with the image contained in the classes vanishing a.e. outside $U$, and $\|R_Ug\|_{W^{1,p}(\Omega)}\le C(\Omega,p,U)\|g\|_{W^{\theta,p}(\partial\Omega)}$. The right inverse is not unique and no canonical choice is claimed.
projection.strategy: Patch the local half-space lifts of [[thm-half-space-lift-by-normal-mollification]]: choose a finite boundary atlas contained in the prescribed collar $U$, a subordinate finite partition of unity on $\partial\Omega$ for the atlas, and for each chart transport the flat lift of the localised datum, multiplied by a smooth cutoff supported in the chart and in $U$. The flat estimate controls each transported piece in $W^{1,p}$ through [[lem-c-k-boundary-flattening-preserves-wkp-locally]] and [[lem-fractional-boundary-norm-is-independent-of-atlas]]; the finitely many pieces agree on overlaps up to null sets and paste by [[lem-sobolev-pasting-across-an-overlap]] and [[lem-trace-commutes-with-smooth-boundary-cutoffs-and-charts]]. The resulting operator is linear and bounded, and $T\circ R=\mathrm{id}$ because on each chart the local lift has trace equal to the localised datum and the partition sums to one on $\partial\Omega$. The same construction with the atlas chosen inside $U$ gives the collar-supported version. The Axiom of Choice is carried through the density, trace and partition interfaces; the finite patch uses no further choice.

projection.title: The trace of a one-dimensional Sobolev function is the pair of endpoint values
projection.statement: Assume Countable Choice. Let $I=(a,b)$ be a bounded interval, $1\le p<\infty$ and $u\in W^{1,p}(I;\mathbb K)$ with unique absolutely continuous representative $u^*$ ([[cor-one-dimensional-w-one-p-functions-have-absolutely-continuous-representatives]]). Identify the boundary $\partial I=\{a,b\}$ with its counting measure. Then the trace of $u$ is the pair $\bigl(u^*(a),u^*(b)\bigr)\in\mathbb K^2$, this pair depends only on the class of $u$, and $u\in W_0^{1,p}(I)$ if and only if $u^*(a)=u^*(b)=0$. On $(0,1)$: for $u(x)=x(1-x)$ one has $u^*=u$ and $Tu=(0,0)$, while for $u\equiv1$ one has $Tu=(1,1)\ne0$.
projection.strategy: The endpoint values of the absolutely continuous representative are well defined and, by [[lem-one-dimensional-sobolev-endpoint-estimate]], they are controlled by the $W^{1,p}$ norm, so the map $u\mapsto(u^*(a),u^*(b))$ is a linear contraction up to a constant and is independent of the chosen representative. The zero-trace statement in one dimension is proved directly, without the higher-dimensional chart theorem: test functions of $C_c^\infty(I)$ have both endpoint values zero, and the endpoint pairing is continuous by the estimate, so every class in the closure has zero endpoints; conversely, if $u^*(a)=u^*(b)=0$ then the zero extension of $u$ is absolutely continuous on every compact subinterval of $\mathbb R$ with $L^p$ derivative (the ACL characterisation [[thm-acl-characterisation-of-w-one-p]] applied on $\mathbb R$), and mollifying that extension with the standard mollifier produces test functions on $I$ converging to $u$ in $W^{1,p}(I)$. The two worked functions are checked by direct differentiation. Countable Choice is carried by the ACL interface.

projection.title: Boundary point values are not a function of the interior $L^p$ class
projection.statement: Assume Countable Choice. On $\Omega=(0,1)^n$ the functions $f=0$ and $\tilde f=\mathbf 1_{\partial\Omega}$ differ only on the Lebesgue-null set $\partial\Omega$, so they represent the same element of $L^p(\Omega)$ and of $W^{k,p}(\Omega)$ for every $k,p$; yet their classical restrictions to $\partial\Omega$ are the zero function and the constant-one function, which are different on the whole boundary, while $Tf=T\tilde f=0$ by [[thm-lp-trace-operator-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]]. Even without changing representatives, an $L^p$ class need not have finite boundary values: $x\mapsto(1-|x|)^{-1/4}$ lies in $L^2(B(0,1))$ but is unbounded on every neighbourhood of the boundary. Hence pointwise evaluation on $\partial\Omega$ is not well defined from the interior class alone, and the trace operator is the correct replacement; the operator itself is well defined on classes.
projection.strategy: The coincidence of the two classes is the definition of $L^p$ as a quotient by null functions ([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]) and the fact that $\partial\Omega$ is a Lebesgue-null set with empty interior. The classical restrictions differ at every boundary point, since $\tilde f|_{\partial\Omega}\equiv1$. The trace of both classes vanishes because the defining clause of [[thm-lp-trace-operator-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]] gives $T$ applied to the continuous function $0$. The unbounded example is the standard $L^2$ function $(1-|x|)^{-1/4}$ on the unit ball, whose $L^2$ norm is finite while no neighbourhood of $\partial\Omega$ has a finite essential bound. No choice beyond Countable Choice is used.

projection.title: A jump boundary datum is outside the trace range for $p\ge2$
projection.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^2$ be a bounded $C^1$ domain with a boundary chart whose image contains a straight segment, and let $g=\mathbf 1_{(0,1)}$ be the jump function on that segment, extended by zero. Then $g\in L^p(\partial\Omega)$ for every $p$, but for every $2\le p<\infty$ one has $g\notin W^{1-1/p,p}(\partial\Omega)$: at $p=2$ the chart computation gives $[g]_{1/2,2}^2=2\int_0^1\int_0^\infty(s+t)^{-2}\,ds\,dt=2\int_0^1 t^{-1}\,dt=+\infty$, so the Slobodeckij seminorm of [[def-fractional-slobodeckij-space-on-euclidean-space]] diverges, and by [[thm-sharp-trace-theorem-for-w-one-p]] no $u\in W^{1,p}(\Omega)$ has $Tu=g$. In particular the Dirichlet datum is not arbitrary in $L^p(\partial\Omega)$, and the trace range depends on $p$: for $1<p<2$ the same jump function does belong to $W^{1-1/p,p}$ because $1-1/p<1/p$.
projection.strategy: Compute in the chart (the straight segment is identified with $(0,1)\subset\mathbb R$): the difference $|g(x)-g(y)|$ equals $1$ exactly when one of $x,y$ lies in $(0,1)$ and the other outside, so $[g]_{s,p}^p=2\int_0^1\int_0^\infty(s+t)^{-1-sp}ds\,dt=\frac{2}{sp}\int_0^1(1-t)^{-sp}dt$, finite exactly when $sp<1$. For $p=2$, $s=1/2$ gives $sp=1$ and the integral diverges logarithmically at $t=1$ and $s=0$; for $p>2$, $sp=p-1>1$ and it diverges; for $1<p<2$, $sp=p-1<1$ and it converges. Apply [[thm-sharp-trace-theorem-for-w-one-p]] to translate the failure of the seminorm into non-membership in the trace range. The boundary chart and the surface measure are those of the page conventions; no choice beyond the cited interfaces is used.

projection.title: Zero trace, zero boundary values and zero extension agree on an interval
projection.statement: Assume Countable Choice. Let $I=(0,1)$ and $1\le p<\infty$. For $u\in W^{1,p}(I)$ with absolutely continuous representative $u^*$ the following are equivalent: (i) $Tu=0$; (ii) $u^*(0)=u^*(1)=0$; (iii) $u\in W_0^{1,p}(I)$; (iv) the extension of $u$ by zero belongs to $W^{1,p}(\mathbb R)$. For $u(x)=x(1-x)$ all four hold: the zero extension is the continuous function equal to $x(1-x)$ on $[0,1]$ and $0$ outside, with weak derivative $1-2x$ on $(0,1)$ and $0$ outside. For $u\equiv1$ all four fail, and the zero extension has distributional derivative $\delta_0-\delta_1$.
projection.strategy: (i)$\Leftrightarrow$(ii) is the one-dimensional trace identification of [[ex-trace-of-an-ac-sobolev-function-on-an-interval]]. (ii)$\Leftrightarrow$(iv): the zero extension is absolutely continuous across the endpoints exactly when both endpoint values vanish, and then its derivative is the zero extension of $u'$, so the ACL characterisation [[thm-acl-characterisation-of-w-one-p]] gives membership in $W^{1,p}(\mathbb R)$. (ii)$\Rightarrow$(iii): cut off $u$ by a fixed interior cutoff $\eta_\delta$ equal to one on $[\delta,1-\delta]$; the endpoint vanishing gives $\|u(1-\eta_\delta)\|_{W^{1,p}(I)}\to0$ because $|u(x)|\le x^{1-1/p}\|u'\|_{L^p}$ near an endpoint, and the compactly supported pieces are approximated by test functions using [[lem-compact-support-zero-extension-in-wkp]] and mollification. (iii)$\Rightarrow$(ii): test functions have both endpoint values zero and the endpoint pairing is continuous, so the property passes to the closure. The two concrete functions are checked by direct differentiation: $x(1-x)$ vanishes at both endpoints, while $\mathbf 1_{(0,1)}$ has the displayed Dirac derivative by integration by parts against test functions (the companion PDE-12 counterexample records the computation). Countable Choice is carried by the ACL and extension interfaces.

projection.title: Fourier pairing for a finite measure and Schwartz data
projection.statement: Assume Countable Choice. Let $\mu$ be a finite complex Borel measure on $\mathbb R^n$ and let $F,G\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^n)$. (i) $\int_{\mathbb R^n}(G\mu)^\vee(x)\overline{F(x)}\,dx=\int_{\mathbb R^n}G(\omega)\overline{\widehat F(\omega)}\,d\mu(\omega)$, where $(G\mu)^\vee(x)=\int e^{2\pi ix\cdot\omega}G(\omega)\,d\mu(\omega)$. (ii) Writing $\check\mu(x):=\widehat\mu(-x)=\int e^{2\pi ix\cdot\omega}\,d\mu(\omega)$, one has $(\widehat F\,\mu)^\vee=F*\check\mu$ as everywhere-defined bounded continuous functions. (iii) $|\check\mu(x)|\le|\mu|(\mathbb R^n)$ for every $x$, and $\check\mu$ is uniformly continuous.

projection.title: TT-star reduces extension to convolution with the surface-measure transform
projection.statement: Assume Countable Choice. Let $\mu$ be a finite complex Borel measure on $\mathbb R^n$, let $E_\mu g=(g\mu)^\vee$ for $g\in L^1(\mu)\cap L^2(\mu)$, and let $E_\mu^*F$ be the restriction of $\widehat F$ to $\operatorname{supp}\mu$ for $F\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^n)$. Then $E_\mu E_\mu^*F=F*\check\mu$ for every $F\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^n)$, and for every $1\le p\le\infty$, $\|\widehat F\|_{L^2(\mu)}^2=\langle(\widehat F\mu)^\vee,F\rangle=\langle F*\check\mu,F\rangle\le\|F\|_{L^p}\|F*\check\mu\|_{L^{p'}}$. In particular, for a compact hypersurface $S$ with surface measure $\sigma$, a bound on $\|F*\check\sigma\|_{L^{p'}}$ bounds $\|\widehat F\|_{L^2(\sigma)}$.

projection.strategy: Apply the pairing identity with $G=\widehat F$ to identify the squared $L^2(\mu)$ norm with $\langle(\widehat F\mu)^\vee,F\rangle$, then the convolution identity to replace $(\widehat F\mu)^\vee$ by $F*\check\mu$, and Holder to bound the pairing.

projection.title: Knapp rules out extension below the Tomas exponent
projection.statement: Let $n\ge2$ and let $q<2(n+1)/(n-1)$. For every $C>0$ there is $\delta\in(0,1]$ such that the spherical cap data $g=\mathbf 1_{C_\delta}\in L^2(\sigma)$ satisfy $\|Eg\|_{L^q(\mathbb R^n)}>C\|g\|_{L^2(\sigma)}$. Hence no extension estimate $E:L^2(S^{n-1})\to L^q(\mathbb R^n)$ holds below the Stein-Tomas exponent, and consequently no restriction estimate $R:L^p(\mathbb R^n)\to L^2(S^{n-1})$ holds for $p>2(n+1)/(n+3)$.

projection.strategy: Combine the cap concentration with the slab volume, compute $\|Eg\|_q\gtrsim\delta^{n-1-(n+1)/q}$ and $\|g\|_2\asymp\delta^{(n-1)/2}$, and let $\delta\downarrow0$ for $q$ below the Tomas exponent.

projection.title: The one-dimensional endpoint estimate on a bounded interval
projection.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice through the ACL interface of [[thm-acl-characterisation-of-w-one-p]]. Let $I=(a,b)$ be a bounded open interval, $1\le p<\infty$, $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, and let $u\in W^{1,p}(I;\mathbb K)$ with weak derivative $u'$ and unique absolutely continuous representative $u^*$ ([[cor-one-dimensional-w-one-p-functions-have-absolutely-continuous-representatives]]). Then for every $0<\varepsilon<b-a$: (i) if $1<p<\infty$, $|u^*(a)|^p\le 2^{p-1}\bigl(\varepsilon^{-1}\int_a^{a+\varepsilon}|u^*|^p+\varepsilon^{p-1}\int_a^{a+\varepsilon}|u'|^p\bigr)$, and the same inequality holds at $b$ with $(b-\varepsilon,b)$; (ii) if $p=1$, $|u^*(a)|\le\varepsilon^{-1}\int_a^{a+\varepsilon}|u^*|+\int_a^{a+\varepsilon}|u'|$, and likewise at $b$. The endpoint values are those of the absolutely continuous representative and do not depend on the chosen representative of the class.
projection.strategy: For a.e. $t\in(a,a+\varepsilon)$ the absolutely continuous representative satisfies $u^*(a)-u^*(t)=-\int_a^t u'$, hence $|u^*(a)|\le|u^*(t)|+\int_a^{a+\varepsilon}|u'|$. For $p>1$ raise this to the $p$-th power with $|x+y|^p\le 2^{p-1}(|x|^p+|y|^p)$, integrate in $t$ over $(a,a+\varepsilon)$, divide by $\varepsilon$, and bound $\int_a^{a+\varepsilon}\bigl(\int_a^{a+\varepsilon}|u'|\bigr)^p=\varepsilon\bigl(\int_a^{a+\varepsilon}|u'|\bigr)^p\le\varepsilon^p\int_a^{a+\varepsilon}|u'|^p$ by Holder. For $p=1$ integrate the unsquared inequality. The capital-$C$ form used later is $\varepsilon|u^*(a)|^p\le C_p\bigl(\int_a^{a+\varepsilon}|u^*|^p+\varepsilon^p\int_a^{a+\varepsilon}|u'|^p\bigr)$. The ACL and FTC interfaces carry the Axiom of Choice; no further choice is used.

projection.title: The half-space trace estimate and the half-space trace operator
projection.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $n\ge2$, $d=n-1$, $1\le p<\infty$, $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, and let $H=\{x=(x',x_n)\in\mathbb R^n:x_n>0\}$ with $\partial H=\mathbb R^d\times\{0\}$. (i) For every $u\in C(\overline H)\cap W^{1,p}(H;\mathbb K)$ with compact support, the classical boundary function $g=u(\cdot,0)$ satisfies $|g(x')|^p\le p\int_0^\infty|u(x',t)|^{p-1}\,|\partial_nu(x',t)|\,dt$ for a.e. $x'\in\mathbb R^d$, hence $\|g\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^d)}^p\le p\,\|u\|_{L^p(H)}^{p-1}\|\partial_nu\|_{L^p(H)}\le p\,\|u\|_{W^{1,p}(H)}^p$. For every $h>0$ the strip form $h\,|g(x')|^p\le C_p\bigl(\int_0^h|u(x',t)|^pdt+h^p\int_0^h|\partial_nu(x',t)|^pdt\bigr)$ holds for a.e. $x'$. (ii) There is a unique bounded linear operator $T_+:W^{1,p}(H;\mathbb K)\to L^p(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb K)$ with $T_+u=u(\cdot,0)$ for every compactly supported $u\in C(\overline H)\cap W^{1,p}(H)$, and $\|T_+u\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^d)}\le C(n,p)\|u\|_{W^{1,p}(H)}$; it is the unique bounded extension of classical restriction, and $T_+u$ depends only on the a.e. class of $u$.
projection.strategy: For (i), fix a representative continuous on $\overline H$; for a.e. $x'$ the section $t\mapsto u(x',t)$ is absolutely continuous on $(0,\infty)$ by the ACL theorem, and since $u$ has compact support, $|g(x')|^p=-\int_0^\infty\partial_t(|u(x',t)|^p)\,dt=-p\int_0^\infty|u|^{p-2}\operatorname{Re}(\overline u\,\partial_nu)dt\le p\int_0^\infty|u|^{p-1}|\partial_nu|\,dt$. Integrate in $x'$, apply Holder with exponents $p/(p-1)$ and $p$, and use $\|\partial_nu\|_p\le\|u\|_{W^{1,p}(H)}$. The strip form integrates the one-dimensional endpoint estimate [[lem-one-dimensional-sobolev-endpoint-estimate]] along the normal section. For (ii), classical restriction is defined on compactly supported smooth functions and is uniformly bounded by (i); that subspace is dense in $W^{1,p}(H)$ because a cutoff in $|x|$ reduces to the bounded domains $H\cap B_R$, where [[thm-smooth-up-to-the-boundary-density-on-smooth-domains]] applies. Apply the bounded-extension property of a dense subspace ([[thm-completion-universal-property-for-bounded-linear-maps]]); uniqueness is immediate. The Axiom of Choice is carried through the density interface used to reach all classes.

projection.title: The trace commutes with smooth cutoffs and is chart local
projection.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a bounded $C^1$ domain, $1\le p<\infty$, and let $T$ be the trace operator of [[thm-lp-trace-operator-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]]. (i) If $\eta\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb K)$, then $T(\eta u)=(\eta|_{\partial\Omega})\,Tu$ in $L^p(\partial\Omega)$ for every $u\in W^{1,p}(\Omega)$, and $\|T(\eta u)\|_{L^p(\partial\Omega)}\le C_\eta\|u\|_{W^{1,p}(\Omega)}$. (ii) If $\Omega'\subseteq\Omega$ is open and $\partial\Omega\cap\partial\Omega'$ is relatively open in $\partial\Omega$, then $(Tu)|_{\partial\Omega\cap\partial\Omega'}=T_{\Omega'}(u|_{\Omega'})$ a.e. for every $u\in W^{1,p}(\Omega)$, where $T_{\Omega'}$ is the trace operator relative to $\Omega'$; in particular the trace is local and compatible with restrictions to subdomains. (iii) If a boundary chart $\Phi$ flattens a neighbourhood of a boundary point, then for $u$ supported in the interior of that chart the transported trace equals $T_+(u\circ\Phi^{-1})$ and the corresponding boundary $L^p$ norms agree up to the chart Jacobian.
projection.strategy: Both identities are classical for smooth functions. Approximate a general $u$ by restrictions of $C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^n)$ functions in the $W^{1,p}$ norm ([[thm-smooth-up-to-the-boundary-density-on-smooth-domains]]), use the product rule [[lem-weak-leibniz-rule-with-a-smooth-factor]] and the continuity of $T$ to pass to the limit in (i); the multiplier $\eta|_{\partial\Omega}$ is continuous on the compact boundary, and Holder gives the stated bound, using [[lem-bounded-restriction-and-cutoff-localisation-in-sobolev-spaces]] for the localisation. Part (ii) follows by testing with cutoffs supported in the common boundary neighbourhood and applying the chartwise definition in part (iii); the transported boundary measure is the chart surface measure, which is chart independent by the page's surface-measure convention. The Axiom of Choice is carried by the density interface.

projection.title: The Gauss-Green integration-by-parts formula with Sobolev traces
projection.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge2$, be a bounded $C^1$ domain, $1<p<\infty$, $p'=p/(p-1)$, $u\in W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$, $v\in W^{1,p'}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$, and let $T$ be the trace of [[thm-lp-trace-operator-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]] with $
u$ the outward normal of [[def-bounded-c-one-domain-boundary-charts-and-outward-normal]]. Then for every $i=1,\dots,n$, $\int_\Omega u\,\partial_iv\,dx=-\int_\Omega(\partial_iu)v\,dx+\int_{\partial\Omega}(Tu)(Tv)\,
u_i\,dS$, and all three integrals are finite. If $u,v\in C^1(\overline\Omega)$, the boundary term is the classical $\int_{\partial\Omega}uv\,
u_i\,dS$ of the divergence theorem [[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-c-one-euclidean-domains]] applied to the field $uv\,e_i$; when $u=\partial_
u w$ this is the classical normal-derivative boundary term of [[def-classical-normal-derivative]].
projection.strategy: For $u,v\in C^1(\overline\Omega)$ the identity is the divergence theorem applied to the field $uv\,e_i$ on the bounded $C^1$ domain. For general $u,v$ choose $u_k\to u$ in $W^{1,p}(\Omega)$ and $v_k\to v$ in $W^{1,p'}(\Omega)$ with $u_k,v_k$ restrictions of $C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^n)$ functions ([[thm-smooth-up-to-the-boundary-density-on-smooth-domains]]), so that $Tu_k\to Tu$ and $Tv_k\to Tv$ in the respective boundary $L^p$ spaces. The volume pairings converge by Holder, $\int_\Omega|u_k\partial_iv_k-u\partial_iv|\le\|u_k-u\|_p\|\partial_iv_k\|_{p'}+\|u\|_p\|\partial_iv_k-\partial_iv\|_{p'}\to0$, and the boundary pairings converge by Holder on $\partial\Omega$ with exponents $p,p'$ ([[thm-holder-inequality-for-integrals]]), the boundary measure being finite. All boundary terms are in $L^1(\partial\Omega)$ since $Tu\in L^p$ and $Tv\in L^{p'}$. The Axiom of Choice is carried by the density and trace interfaces.

projection.title: The kernel of the trace is the closure of the test functions
projection.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge2$, be a bounded $C^1$ domain and $1\le p<\infty$. Then the kernel of the trace operator of [[thm-lp-trace-operator-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]] equals the zero-boundary Sobolev space: $\{u\in W^{1,p}(\Omega):Tu=0\}=W_0^{1,p}(\Omega)$, the $W^{1,p}$-closure of $C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ ([[def-wkp-zero-as-a-sobolev-closure]]).
projection.strategy: Forward: for $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ the classical restriction to $\partial\Omega$ vanishes, so $T\varphi=0$ by [[lem-sobolev-trace-agrees-with-continuous-boundary-values]], and $T$ is continuous, so the identity passes to the $W^{1,p}$-closure. Conversely let $Tu=0$. Localise with the finite ambient partition of [[lem-finite-ambient-partitions-for-euclidean-boundary-integration]] and an interior cutoff, and for each boundary piece $w=\chi_ju$ flatten to a compactly supported $W^{1,p}(H)$ function with zero flat trace ([[lem-c-k-boundary-flattening-preserves-wkp-locally]], [[lem-trace-commutes-with-smooth-boundary-cutoffs-and-charts]]). Define $\bar w$ on $\mathbb R^n$ to be $w$ on $H$ and $0$ below the boundary. The half-space case of [[thm-sobolev-gauss-green-formula-on-c-one-domains]] (applied on a large half-ball containing the support) shows, for every test function $\varphi$, $\int_{\mathbb R^n}\bar w\,\partial_i\varphi=-\int_{\mathbb R^n}\bar v_i\,\varphi$ where $\bar v_i$ is the zero extension of $\partial_iw$: the boundary term at $x_n=0$ contains the flat trace $T_+w=0$ and the spherical part is outside the support. Hence $\bar w\in W^{1,p}(\mathbb R^n)$ with the zero-extended weak derivatives. Translate, $w_\varepsilon(x):=\bar w(x-\varepsilon e_n)$, so that $w_\varepsilon\to w$ in $W^{1,p}(H)$ by translation continuity, and mollify at scale $\delta<\varepsilon/2$: $\rho_\delta*w_\varepsilon\in C_c^\infty(H)$ with $\rho_\delta*w_\varepsilon\to w$ in $W^{1,p}(H)$ ([[cor-compactly-supported-smooth-functions-are-dense-in-wkp-of-rn]]). Pulling these approximations back through the chart gives $C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ functions converging to $\chi_ju$, and the interior piece is mollified directly; a finite sum of $C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ approximations converges to $u$, so $u\in W_0^{1,p}(\Omega)$. The Axiom of Choice is carried by the density, flattening and partition interfaces; the extension-by-zero step is otherwise explicit.

projection.statement: Assume Countable Choice for the measure interfaces. Let $d\ge1$, $0<s<1$, $1\le p<\infty$ and $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. For a measurable $g:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb K$ put $[g]_{s,p}:=\bigl(\int_{\mathbb R^d}\int_{\mathbb R^d}|g(x)-g(y)|^p|x-y|^{-d-sp}\,dx\,dy\bigr)^{1/p}\in[0,\infty]$, with the integrand understood as $0$ on the diagonal $x=y$. The Gagliardo-Slobodeckij space is $W^{s,p}(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb K):=\{g\in L^p(\mathbb R^d):[g]_{s,p}<\infty\}$, normed by $\|g\|_{W^{s,p}}:=\|g\|_{L^p}+[g]_{s,p}$. The seminorm and the space are meant to depend only on the almost-everywhere class; representative independence is recorded as the first clause of the well-definedness lemma on this page. On this page the exponent used is $s=\theta:=1-1/p\in(0,1)$, which is the trace exponent for $1<p<\infty$.
projection.strategy: Unpack the double integral as an integral over the completed product measure on $\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R^d$ ([[thm-tonelli-and-fubini-for-completed-product-measures]]); the diagonal is a null set, so the convention is harmless, and the integral is a nonnegative extended integral of a measurable function ([[def-nonnegative-lebesgue-integral]]). Membership and norm are stated on classes ([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]); representative independence is not assumed here but proved as the first clause of [[lem-slobodeckij-seminorm-is-well-defined]]. Only the countable-choice measure interfaces are used; the definition itself is choice free.

projection.title: The coordinate-direction form of the Slobodeckij seminorm
projection.statement: Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\ge1$, $0<s<1$, $1\le p<\infty$, and let $g$ be measurable. Then, with $e_1,\dots,e_d$ the canonical basis, $[g]_{s,p}^p\asymp_{d,p,s}\sum_{i=1}^d\int_0^\infty h^{-1-sp}\int_{\mathbb R^d}|g(x+he_i)-g(x)|^p\,dx\,dh$, in the sense that both sides are finite simultaneously and the two quantities are comparable by constants depending only on $d,p,s$. For the trace exponent $s=\theta=1-1/p$ the weight is $h^{-p}$, because $1+p\theta=p$.
projection.strategy: By translation invariance of Lebesgue measure ([[thm-integrals-are-invariant-under-measure-preserving-maps]]) substitute $y=x+h$ in the inner integral, so $[g]_{s,p}^p=\int_{\mathbb R^d}\|\tau_hg-g\|_{L^p}^p|h|^{-d-sp}dh$. Polar coordinates ([[thm-polar-coordinates-formula-for-lebesgue-measure]]) turn this into the integral over radii of the spherical mean of $\|\tau_{r\omega}g-g\|_p^p$ against $r^{-1-sp}dr$. Cover the unit sphere by the finitely many coordinate caps $\{|\omega_i|\ge c_d\}$; on a cap with $\omega_i\ge c_d$ the increment $h=r\omega$ satisfies $r\le c_d^{-1}h_i$ with $h_i=r\omega_i$, so the full increment is controlled by the coordinate increment $h_ie_i$ plus the tangential remainder of size $O(r)$, and iterating over the $d$ caps gives the upper comparison; the lower comparison is immediate because the coordinate directions form a subset of all directions. The identity $1+p\theta=p$ at $\theta=1-1/p$ converts the weight. Only countable-choice measure interfaces are used.

projection.title: The Hardy inequality for the averaging operator on the half-line
projection.statement: Let $1<p<\infty$ and let $f:(0,\infty)\to[0,\infty]$ be measurable. Then $\bigl(\int_0^\infty\bigl(t^{-1}\int_0^tf(s)\,ds\bigr)^pdt\bigr)^{1/p}\le\frac{p}{p-1}\bigl(\int_0^\infty f^p\bigr)^{1/p}$; equivalently $\int_0^\infty t^{-p}\bigl(\int_0^tf\bigr)^pdt\le\bigl(\frac{p}{p-1}\bigr)^p\int_0^\infty f^p$, with $+\infty$ on either side allowed, and the constant $p/(p-1)$ is sharp. The same inequality holds on $(0,T)$ for every $0<T<\infty$ when $f$ is supported in $(0,T)$, with the same constant.
projection.strategy: Assume first that $f$ is continuous with compact support and put $F(t)=\int_0^tf$. Integrate by parts on $(\delta,T)$ against the primitive of $t^{-p}$, namely $-t^{1-p}/(p-1)$: $\int_\delta^TF^pt^{-p}dt=\bigl[-F^pt^{1-p}/(p-1)\bigr]_\delta^T+\frac{p}{p-1}\int_\delta^TF^{p-1}ft^{1-p}dt$. The boundary term at $\delta\downarrow0$ vanishes because $F(t)\le t^{1-1/p}\|f\|_p$ on $(0,t)$, and the term at $T\uparrow\infty$ vanishes because $F$ is eventually constant while $t^{1-p}\to0$. Holders inequality with exponents $p/(p-1)$ and $p$ applied to the product $(F/t)^{p-1}\cdot f$ gives $\int F^{p-1}ft^{1-p}\le\bigl(\int(F/t)^p\bigr)^{(p-1)/p}\|f\|_p$; writing $I=\int_0^\infty(F/t)^pdt$ yields $I\le\frac{p}{p-1}I^{(p-1)/p}\|f\|_p$, hence $I^{1/p}\le\frac{p}{p-1}\|f\|_p$. The general measurable case follows by monotone approximation; the $(0,T)$ case by extending $f$ by zero. The constant is sharp on powers $f(t)=t^{\alpha}$ near the endpoint. No choice beyond Countable Choice for the integral interfaces is used.

projection.title: Compactly supported smooth functions are dense in Slobodeckij spaces
projection.statement: Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\ge1$, $0<s<1$ and $1\le p<\infty$. Then $C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^d)$ is dense in $W^{s,p}(\mathbb R^d)$: for every $g\in W^{s,p}(\mathbb R^d)$ and every $\varepsilon>0$ there is $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^d)$ with $\|g-\varphi\|_{W^{s,p}}<\varepsilon$.
projection.strategy: First truncate: choose $\eta\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^d)$ equal to $1$ near the origin and put $\eta_R(x)=\eta(x/R)$. The functions $\eta_Rg$ converge to $g$ in $L^p$ and in the seminorm: on the region $\{|x|\le R\}$ the functions agree, and the remaining double integral over the escaping region is dominated by $2^{p-1}(|g(x)|^p+|g(y)|^p)$-type integrands whose contribution tends to $0$ by dominated convergence in the double integral. Then mollify: for $\varphi\in W^{s,p}(\mathbb R^d)$ of compact support and the standard mollifier $\rho_\varepsilon$, the difference $|(\rho_\varepsilon*\varphi)(x)-(\rho_\varepsilon*\varphi)(y)|$ is at most $\int\rho_\varepsilon(z)|\varphi(x-z)-\varphi(y-z)|dz$, whence $[\rho_\varepsilon*\varphi]_{s,p}\le[\varphi]_{s,p}$ and $[\rho_\varepsilon*\varphi-\varphi]_{s,p}^p\le\int\rho_\varepsilon(z)\int\int|\varphi(x-z)-\varphi(x)-\varphi(y-z)+\varphi(y)|^p|x-y|^{-d-sp}dxdydz$, which tends to $0$ by translation continuity in $L^p$ ([[thm-translation-is-continuous-in-l-p-for-one-le-p-less-infinity]]) and dominated convergence. Together with [[thm-l-one-approximate-identities-converge-in-l-p]] this gives $\rho_\varepsilon*\varphi\to\varphi$ in $W^{s,p}$. Only countable-choice interfaces are used.

projection.title: The fractional Sobolev space on a compact C^1 boundary
projection.statement: Assume Countable Choice and the boundary conventions of [[def-bounded-c-one-domain-boundary-charts-and-outward-normal]]. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge2$, be a bounded $C^1$ domain, $0<s<1$ and $1\le p<\infty$. Fix a finite family of boundary charts $\Phi_j:U_j\to V_j$, whose restrictions parametrise $\partial\Omega\cap U_j$ over open sets of $\mathbb R^{n-1}$, and a subordinate finite ambient partition $\chi_j$ ([[lem-finite-ambient-partitions-for-euclidean-boundary-integration]]). For a Borel function $g:\partial\Omega\to\mathbb K$ set $\|g\|_{W^{s,p}(\partial\Omega)}:=\sum_j\|(\chi_jg)\circ\Phi_j^{-1}\|_{W^{s,p}(\mathbb R^{n-1})}$, where the chart representation is taken in graph coordinates. Then $W^{s,p}(\partial\Omega;\mathbb K)$ is the set of $L^p(\partial\Omega)$ classes with finite norm. The definition is independent of the atlas and partition up to equivalent norms; the atlas-independence lemma on this page proves the invariance.
projection.strategy: Each chart contributes the Euclidean Slobodeckij norm of [[def-fractional-slobodeckij-space-on-euclidean-space]] applied to the local graph representation; the finite sum over the partition covers the compact boundary, and the surface-measure description of [[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]] fixes which functions are a.e. equal on the boundary. Well-definedness on classes follows from the Euclidean representative independence, and atlas independence is proved separately in [[lem-fractional-boundary-norm-is-independent-of-atlas]]. Countable Choice is carried through the measure interfaces; the finitely many charts and the partition use no further choice.

projection.title: Chart independence of the fractional boundary norm
projection.statement: Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega$ be a bounded $C^1$ domain, $0<s<1$ and $1\le p<\infty$. (i) If $\Psi:V\to V'$ is a $C^1$ diffeomorphism between open subsets of $\mathbb R^{n-1}$ whose derivatives in both directions are bounded, then $\|u\circ\Psi\|_{W^{s,p}(V)}\le C(\Psi,s,p)\|u\|_{W^{s,p}(V')}$ and symmetrically; in particular the Slobodeckij norm is preserved up to equivalence by bi-Lipschitz $C^1$ coordinate changes. (ii) Consequently two finite chart families with subordinate partitions, as in [[def-fractional-sobolev-space-on-a-compact-c-one-boundary]], define equivalent norms on $\partial\Omega$, so $W^{s,p}(\partial\Omega)$ is well defined.
projection.strategy: For (i) split the double integral for $u\circ\Psi$ into pairs with $|x-y|\le r$ and $|x-y|>r$ for a fixed $r>0$. On the near-diagonal part change variables with [[thm-c-one-change-of-variables-for-nonnegative-lebesgue-measurable-functions]] and use the bi-Lipschitz bounds $c_1|x-y|\le|\Psi(x)-\Psi(y)|\le c_2|x-y|$ together with the mean-value bound $|u(\Psi(x))-u(\Psi(y))|^p/|\Psi(x)-\Psi(y)|^{d+sp}\le C|x-y|^{-d-sp}|u|^{\text{difference}}$-type control; on the far part use $|u(\Psi(x))-u(\Psi(y))|^p\le2^{p-1}(|u(\Psi(x))|^p+|u(\Psi(y))|^p)$ and the finiteness of $\int_{|h|>r}|h|^{-d-sp}dh$ together with the change-of-variables formula, giving the $L^p$ term. This is the standard 'split at the length scale' argument; all constants depend on the chart data, $s$, $p$ and the dimension. Part (ii) follows by composing the finitely many chart transitions, each of which is such a diffeomorphism on the overlaps. Only countable-choice measure interfaces are used; the finitely many charts and overlaps are handled without further choice.

projection.title: A bounded right inverse of the half-space trace by normal mollification
projection.statement: Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\ge1$, $1<p<\infty$, $\theta=1-1/p$. Fix $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^d)$ with $\int\varphi=1$, put $\varphi_t(y)=t^{-d}\varphi(y/t)$ and $\psi:=-\sum_i\partial_i(y_i\varphi)$, so that $\int\psi=0$ and $\partial_t(g*\varphi_t)=t^{-1}(g*\psi_t)$; fix $\eta\in C_c^\infty([0,\infty))$ with $\eta\equiv1$ on $[0,1]$ and $\eta\equiv0$ on $[2,\infty)$. For $g\in W^{\theta,p}(\mathbb R^d)$ define $R_+g(x,t):=\eta(t)(g*\varphi_t)(x)$ for $x\in\mathbb R^d$, $t>0$. Then $R_+g\in W^{1,p}(\mathbb R^d\times(0,\infty))$ with $\partial_t(R_+g)=\eta'(t)(g*\varphi_t)+\eta(t)t^{-1}(g*\psi_t)$ and $\partial_{x_i}(R_+g)=\eta(t)(g*\partial_i\varphi_t)$, and $\|R_+g\|_{W^{1,p}}\le C(d,p,\varphi,\eta)\|g\|_{W^{\theta,p}(\mathbb R^d)}$. Moreover $T_+(R_+g)=g$, so $R_+$ is a bounded linear right inverse of the half-space trace $T_+$.
projection.strategy: Define $R_+$ first on the dense subspace $C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^d)$ ([[lem-smooth-compactly-supported-functions-are-dense-in-slobodeckij-spaces]]), where the construction is the source's: with the standard mollifier $\rho$ and $\varphi_t=\rho_t$, put $v(x,t)=g*\rho_{|t|}(x)$ and $R_+g(x,t)=v(x,t)\eta(t)$. This is linear, smooth off $t=0$, continuous up to $t=0$ with $R_+g(\cdot,0)=g$, and Young's inequality gives $\|R_+g\|_p\le C\|g\|_p$; the displayed derivatives are classical. The tangential derivatives are convolutions with the mean-zero kernels $\partial_i\rho_t$, and the normal derivative is a convolution with $\partial_t\rho_t$ plus the term $\eta'(t)(g*\rho_t)$; compact support, boundedness by $Ct^{-d}$ on $B(0,t)$ and the mean-zero property make each of them fall under [[lem-mean-zero-kernel-scale-estimate]], so $\int_0^\infty\|DR_+g(\cdot,t)\|_p^pdt\le C([g]_{\theta,p}^p+\|g\|_p^p)$ and $\|R_+g\|_{W^{1,p}}\le C\|g\|_{W^{\theta,p}}$. The trace identity $T_+(R_+g)=g$ holds by [[lem-sobolev-trace-agrees-with-continuous-boundary-values]]. Finally extend $R_+$ to all of $W^{\theta,p}$ by the bounded-extension property of the dense subspace ([[thm-completion-universal-property-for-bounded-linear-maps]], target $W^{1,p}(H)$ a Banach space); the trace identity extends by continuity. Only countable-choice measure, convolution and completion interfaces are used.

projection.title: The sharp trace theorem: boundedness and range in the fractional space
projection.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge2$, be a bounded $C^1$ domain, $1<p<\infty$ and $\theta=1-1/p$, with $W^{\theta,p}(\partial\Omega)$ as in [[def-fractional-sobolev-space-on-a-compact-c-one-boundary]]. Then the trace operator $T$ of [[thm-lp-trace-operator-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]] satisfies $\|Tu\|_{W^{\theta,p}(\partial\Omega)}\le C(\Omega,p)\|u\|_{W^{1,p}(\Omega)}$ for all $u\in W^{1,p}(\Omega)$, and it is onto: $T(W^{1,p}(\Omega))=W^{\theta,p}(\partial\Omega)$. For $p>1$ the range is a strict subset of $L^p(\partial\Omega)$, and the trace is not a compact operator into $W^{\theta,p}(\partial\Omega)$.
projection.strategy: Boundedness: localise with the finite boundary atlas and partition, flatten each piece to the half-space, and apply the half-space bound [[lem-half-space-trace-has-the-fractional-slobodeckij-bound]]; chart transitions preserve the fractional norm up to equivalence by [[lem-fractional-boundary-norm-is-independent-of-atlas]] and the boundary measure is chart independent, so the chartwise bounds sum to the global one. Surjectivity: for $g\in W^{\theta,p}(\partial\Omega)$ use the local half-space lifts of [[thm-half-space-lift-by-normal-mollification]] on the boundary charts, multiply by a subordinate partition of unity on $\partial\Omega$ and transport with the charts to obtain $u\in W^{1,p}(\Omega)$; the pullbacks of the flat lifts have controlled $W^{1,p}$ norms by the chart-flattening estimate [[lem-c-k-boundary-flattening-preserves-wkp-locally]], the pieces paste by [[lem-trace-commutes-with-smooth-boundary-cutoffs-and-charts]], and $Tu=g$ since each local lift reproduces its cutoff multiple of $g$. Strictness and non-compactness: the trace is onto an infinite-dimensional Banach space, so it cannot be compact; and the range is strictly smaller than $L^p(\partial\Omega)$ because the boundary Slobodeckij seminorm is not controlled by the $L^p$ norm (a jump datum gives a divergent seminorm; the companion page records this). The Axiom of Choice is carried through the density, trace and partition interfaces.

projection.title: A bounded right inverse of the trace, supported in a prescribed collar
projection.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge2$, be a bounded $C^1$ domain, $1<p<\infty$, $\theta=1-1/p$, and let $T$ be the trace. Then there is a bounded linear operator $R:W^{\theta,p}(\partial\Omega)\to W^{1,p}(\Omega)$ with $T\circ R=\mathrm{id}_{W^{\theta,p}(\partial\Omega)}$ and $\|Rg\|_{W^{1,p}(\Omega)}\le C(\Omega,p)\|g\|_{W^{\theta,p}(\partial\Omega)}$. Moreover, for every open neighbourhood $U$ of $\partial\Omega$ in $\mathbb R^n$ there is such an operator $R_U$ with the image contained in the classes vanishing a.e. outside $U$, and $\|R_Ug\|_{W^{1,p}(\Omega)}\le C(\Omega,p,U)\|g\|_{W^{\theta,p}(\partial\Omega)}$. The right inverse is not unique and no canonical choice is claimed.
projection.strategy: Patch the local half-space lifts of [[thm-half-space-lift-by-normal-mollification]]: choose a finite boundary atlas contained in the prescribed collar $U$, a subordinate finite partition of unity on $\partial\Omega$ for the atlas, and for each chart transport the flat lift of the localised datum, multiplied by a smooth cutoff supported in the chart and in $U$. The flat estimate controls each transported piece in $W^{1,p}$ through [[lem-c-k-boundary-flattening-preserves-wkp-locally]] and [[lem-fractional-boundary-norm-is-independent-of-atlas]]; the finitely many pieces agree on overlaps up to null sets and paste by [[lem-sobolev-pasting-across-an-overlap]] and [[lem-trace-commutes-with-smooth-boundary-cutoffs-and-charts]]. The resulting operator is linear and bounded, and $T\circ R=\mathrm{id}$ because on each chart the local lift has trace equal to the localised datum and the partition sums to one on $\partial\Omega$. The same construction with the atlas chosen inside $U$ gives the collar-supported version. The Axiom of Choice is carried through the density, trace and partition interfaces; the finite patch uses no further choice.

projection.title: The trace of a one-dimensional Sobolev function is the pair of endpoint values
projection.statement: Assume Countable Choice. Let $I=(a,b)$ be a bounded interval, $1\le p<\infty$ and $u\in W^{1,p}(I;\mathbb K)$ with unique absolutely continuous representative $u^*$ ([[cor-one-dimensional-w-one-p-functions-have-absolutely-continuous-representatives]]). Identify the boundary $\partial I=\{a,b\}$ with its counting measure. Then the trace of $u$ is the pair $\bigl(u^*(a),u^*(b)\bigr)\in\mathbb K^2$, this pair depends only on the class of $u$, and $u\in W_0^{1,p}(I)$ if and only if $u^*(a)=u^*(b)=0$. On $(0,1)$: for $u(x)=x(1-x)$ one has $u^*=u$ and $Tu=(0,0)$, while for $u\equiv1$ one has $Tu=(1,1)\ne0$.
projection.strategy: The endpoint values of the absolutely continuous representative are well defined and, by [[lem-one-dimensional-sobolev-endpoint-estimate]], they are controlled by the $W^{1,p}$ norm, so the map $u\mapsto(u^*(a),u^*(b))$ is a linear contraction up to a constant and is independent of the chosen representative. The zero-trace statement in one dimension is proved directly, without the higher-dimensional chart theorem: test functions of $C_c^\infty(I)$ have both endpoint values zero, and the endpoint pairing is continuous by the estimate, so every class in the closure has zero endpoints; conversely, if $u^*(a)=u^*(b)=0$ then the zero extension of $u$ is absolutely continuous on every compact subinterval of $\mathbb R$ with $L^p$ derivative (the ACL characterisation [[thm-acl-characterisation-of-w-one-p]] applied on $\mathbb R$), and mollifying that extension with the standard mollifier produces test functions on $I$ converging to $u$ in $W^{1,p}(I)$. The two worked functions are checked by direct differentiation. Countable Choice is carried by the ACL interface.

projection.title: Boundary point values are not a function of the interior $L^p$ class
projection.statement: Assume Countable Choice. On $\Omega=(0,1)^n$ the functions $f=0$ and $\tilde f=\mathbf 1_{\partial\Omega}$ differ only on the Lebesgue-null set $\partial\Omega$, so they represent the same element of $L^p(\Omega)$ and of $W^{k,p}(\Omega)$ for every $k,p$; yet their classical restrictions to $\partial\Omega$ are the zero function and the constant-one function, which are different on the whole boundary, while $Tf=T\tilde f=0$ by [[thm-lp-trace-operator-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]]. Even without changing representatives, an $L^p$ class need not have finite boundary values: $x\mapsto(1-|x|)^{-1/4}$ lies in $L^2(B(0,1))$ but is unbounded on every neighbourhood of the boundary. Hence pointwise evaluation on $\partial\Omega$ is not well defined from the interior class alone, and the trace operator is the correct replacement; the operator itself is well defined on classes.
projection.strategy: The coincidence of the two classes is the definition of $L^p$ as a quotient by null functions ([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]) and the fact that $\partial\Omega$ is a Lebesgue-null set with empty interior. The classical restrictions differ at every boundary point, since $\tilde f|_{\partial\Omega}\equiv1$. The trace of both classes vanishes because the defining clause of [[thm-lp-trace-operator-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]] gives $T$ applied to the continuous function $0$. The unbounded example is the standard $L^2$ function $(1-|x|)^{-1/4}$ on the unit ball, whose $L^2$ norm is finite while no neighbourhood of $\partial\Omega$ has a finite essential bound. No choice beyond Countable Choice is used.

projection.title: A jump boundary datum is outside the trace range for $p\ge2$
projection.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^2$ be a bounded $C^1$ domain with a boundary chart whose image contains a straight segment, and let $g=\mathbf 1_{(0,1)}$ be the jump function on that segment, extended by zero. Then $g\in L^p(\partial\Omega)$ for every $p$, but for every $2\le p<\infty$ one has $g\notin W^{1-1/p,p}(\partial\Omega)$: at $p=2$ the chart computation gives $[g]_{1/2,2}^2=2\int_0^1\int_0^\infty(s+t)^{-2}\,ds\,dt=2\int_0^1 t^{-1}\,dt=+\infty$, so the Slobodeckij seminorm of [[def-fractional-slobodeckij-space-on-euclidean-space]] diverges, and by [[thm-sharp-trace-theorem-for-w-one-p]] no $u\in W^{1,p}(\Omega)$ has $Tu=g$. In particular the Dirichlet datum is not arbitrary in $L^p(\partial\Omega)$, and the trace range depends on $p$: for $1<p<2$ the same jump function does belong to $W^{1-1/p,p}$ because $1-1/p<1/p$.
projection.strategy: Compute in the chart (the straight segment is identified with $(0,1)\subset\mathbb R$): the difference $|g(x)-g(y)|$ equals $1$ exactly when one of $x,y$ lies in $(0,1)$ and the other outside, so $[g]_{s,p}^p=2\int_0^1\int_0^\infty(s+t)^{-1-sp}ds\,dt=\frac{2}{sp}\int_0^1(1-t)^{-sp}dt$, finite exactly when $sp<1$. For $p=2$, $s=1/2$ gives $sp=1$ and the integral diverges logarithmically at $t=1$ and $s=0$; for $p>2$, $sp=p-1>1$ and it diverges; for $1<p<2$, $sp=p-1<1$ and it converges. Apply [[thm-sharp-trace-theorem-for-w-one-p]] to translate the failure of the seminorm into non-membership in the trace range. The boundary chart and the surface measure are those of the page conventions; no choice beyond the cited interfaces is used.

projection.title: Zero trace, zero boundary values and zero extension agree on an interval
projection.statement: Assume Countable Choice. Let $I=(0,1)$ and $1\le p<\infty$. For $u\in W^{1,p}(I)$ with absolutely continuous representative $u^*$ the following are equivalent: (i) $Tu=0$; (ii) $u^*(0)=u^*(1)=0$; (iii) $u\in W_0^{1,p}(I)$; (iv) the extension of $u$ by zero belongs to $W^{1,p}(\mathbb R)$. For $u(x)=x(1-x)$ all four hold: the zero extension is the continuous function equal to $x(1-x)$ on $[0,1]$ and $0$ outside, with weak derivative $1-2x$ on $(0,1)$ and $0$ outside. For $u\equiv1$ all four fail, and the zero extension has distributional derivative $\delta_0-\delta_1$.
projection.strategy: (i)$\Leftrightarrow$(ii) is the one-dimensional trace identification of [[ex-trace-of-an-ac-sobolev-function-on-an-interval]]. (ii)$\Leftrightarrow$(iv): the zero extension is absolutely continuous across the endpoints exactly when both endpoint values vanish, and then its derivative is the zero extension of $u'$, so the ACL characterisation [[thm-acl-characterisation-of-w-one-p]] gives membership in $W^{1,p}(\mathbb R)$. (ii)$\Rightarrow$(iii): cut off $u$ by a fixed interior cutoff $\eta_\delta$ equal to one on $[\delta,1-\delta]$; the endpoint vanishing gives $\|u(1-\eta_\delta)\|_{W^{1,p}(I)}\to0$ because $|u(x)|\le x^{1-1/p}\|u'\|_{L^p}$ near an endpoint, and the compactly supported pieces are approximated by test functions using [[lem-compact-support-zero-extension-in-wkp]] and mollification. (iii)$\Rightarrow$(ii): test functions have both endpoint values zero and the endpoint pairing is continuous, so the property passes to the closure. The two concrete functions are checked by direct differentiation: $x(1-x)$ vanishes at both endpoints, while $\mathbf 1_{(0,1)}$ has the displayed Dirac derivative by integration by parts against test functions (the companion PDE-12 counterexample records the computation). Countable Choice is carried by the ACL and extension interfaces.
